title: Do Language Models Trust Their Own Justifications? A Study on Functional Consistency
abstract: arXiv:2610.32665v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been widely adopted in text classification tasks, where they not only output class predictions but also generate explanations that highlight the tokens deemed most relevant for reaching the predicted label. Yet it remains unclear whether these highlighted elements are behaviorally consistent with the model's own predictions under targeted interventions, which we refer to as functional auto-consistency. While much of the literature evaluates the textual plausibility of such explanations, few studies assess their functional consistency with the model's actual behavior. In this work, we propose an experimental framework based on the principle of auto-consistency: if a model identifies certain tokens as decisive, then isolating, removing, or semantically inverting them should produce systematic and interpretable changes in its predictions. translated_title: 语言模型相信自己的解释吗？一项关于功能一致性的研究
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）已被广泛应用于文本分类任务，它们不仅输出类别预测，还会生成解释，突出显示被认为对得出预测标签最相关的词元。然而，这些被突出的元素在针对性干预下是否与模型自身的预测在行为上保持一致——我们将其称为“功能自一致性”——目前仍不清楚。尽管大量文献评估了此类解释的文本合理性，但很少有研究评估其与模型实际行为之间的功能一致性。在本工作中，我们提出了一个基于自一致性原则的实验框架：如果模型认为某些词元是决定性的，那么分离、移除或语义反转这些词元，应当会在其预测中产生系统性的、可解释的变化。我们通过充分性和完整性等指标将这一评估操作化……
tldr: 该研究提出基于“功能自一致性”原则的实验框架，通过分离、移除或语义反转模型所标记的关键词元，检验语言模型生成的解释是否与其真实预测行为在功能上保持一致。
en_tdlr: This study proposes an experimental framework based on the principle of functional auto-consistency, which tests whether LLMs' token-highlighting explanations are functionally consistent with their actual predictions by isolating, removing, or semantically inverting the tokens the models deem decisive.
